name: Prepare Your Mind

positioning.oneLineSummary: Turns prior learning into explicit screening hypotheses without letting pattern recognition become stereotype.
positioning.productLabel: Prepared Mind Lens — based on The Venture Mindset public materials

attribution.display: Based on Ilya Strebulaev's public nine-principle keynote

neutralParaphrase: Investing upfront in domain knowledge, market maps, failure modes, and explicit hypotheses can improve screening speed when opportunities arrive. Prior patterns must remain testable and cannot replace company-specific evidence or become founder stereotypes.

locator.value: Public author excerpt on uncertainty and disruptive innovation

requiredConditions: The domain has repeated opportunities or identifiable hypotheses worth learning in advance.
Pre-existing beliefs can be versioned and compared with later evidence.

requiredEvidence.description: Dated market map, thesis, failure modes, and open questions created before reviewing the company.
Evidence showing how the company confirms, contradicts, or extends prior beliefs.
Recorded change from prior belief, supporting evidence, and remaining uncertainty.

decisionQuestions: What did the firm believe before seeing this company?
Which belief is supported or contradicted by new evidence?
Is fast recognition based on a causal mechanism or superficial similarity?
Which prior failure mode is relevant, and which is not?
What evidence would force the thesis to change?
positiveSignals: Prior hypotheses are dated and were not rewritten after the pitch.
The company-specific update identifies mechanisms rather than labels.
The firm records belief revisions and missed assumptions.
Screening becomes faster without reducing evidence standards.
redFlags: A known logo, pedigree, or pattern substitutes for diligence.
The thesis was written after seeing the desired company.
Contrary evidence is forced into an old template.
The firm cannot identify cases where its prepared view was wrong.
disconfirmingEvidence: Prior patterns repeatedly fail out of sample.
An apparently similar company has a materially different customer or economic mechanism.
The screening framework rejects later winners for the same unexamined reason.
New evidence requires a thesis revision that the team refuses to record.
contraindications: Do not use pattern similarity as formal evidence.
Do not infer founder quality from demographic or prestige patterns.
Do not apply to stable routine decisions where the uncertainty framework adds overhead.

instructions: Load only beliefs timestamped before the current company evidence.
Map new evidence to each prior hypothesis.
Identify superficial pattern matches and causal matches separately.
Record belief revision and unresolved contradictions.
Conclude on learning quality, not deal quality.

sourceReliability.low: Only a secondary prepared-mind summary is available.
sourceReliability.medium: The official keynote supports the rule without full chapter details.
sourceReliability.high: Hashed keynote and reviewed chapter locators converge.

evidenceStrength.medium: Dated prior thesis and one company-specific update.
evidenceStrength.high: Dated hypotheses, repeated updates, belief revisions, and out-of-sample postmortems exist.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Prior thesis and update exist but revision history is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: Prior beliefs, updates, contradictions, and revisions are documented.

applicabilityConfidence.low: The decision is stable and routine.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: Uncertainty exists but the domain is new to the firm.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Repeated high-uncertainty opportunities reward advance learning.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only an intuition can be reconstructed.
judgmentConfidence.medium: Prepared hypotheses improve questions but calibration is unknown.
judgmentConfidence.high: The process demonstrates faster screening and honest revision across cases.

promotionRequirements: Test screening speed and miss rate out of sample.
Audit for pedigree and demographic proxies.
empiricalQualifications: Pattern recognition can encode historical selection bias.
Prepared frameworks can cause confirmation bias.
Learning benefits differ between disruptive and routine settings.

rights.notes: Only neutral paraphrase of public source concepts is stored.

openIssues: Define prepared-thesis versioning with the Framework Registry.
